acceptance_checks: A goal-level completion ledger of the task's own goal contributes both its own path and every `.shiki`-contained path in its evidence array to the derived locks.
A ledger whose goal_id is foreign contributes nothing.
A ledger whose task_id is set and differs from the task's id contributes nothing.
A goal-level ledger whose evidence ref resolves outside `.shiki` contributes nothing.
An end-to-end closeout-shaped case with three named-file task locks plus a completion ledger and scorecard returns no files-outside-locks blocker.
tests/test_completion_lock_scope.py exists and covers all of the above.
bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh and bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh stay green without being modified.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: Widening any task's stored locks or reintroducing a `.shiki/**` glob
Accepting a ledger whose goal_id differs from the task's goal_id
Accepting a ledger whose task_id is set and differs from the task's id
Removing the `.shiki`-subtree containment check on derived evidence paths
Touching scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh or scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh (held by other tasks)

findings.detail: The loosened bound lets a same-goal ledger with empty task_id contribute its evidence refs to effective locks. As before this change (which already applied to own-task ledgers), a PR that authors such a ledger could cite arbitrary .shiki-contained paths in its evidence array to widen coverage. This is not introduced by this task and is defended in depth by the planned mirror-scope rule R-02 (T-...ee01f3c4, status planned) which blocks modification/deletion of foreign mirror records regardless of locks. No action required for this change.
findings.title: Evidence-ref expansion can reference arbitrary in-.shiki paths via a self-authored same-goal ledger (pre-existing, out of scope)

scope:
One change in `scripts/mergegate_check.py`, inside `_derive_task_mirror_locks`. The ledger-expansion bound is currently:

    if str(entry.get("goal_id") or "") != goal_id or str(entry.get("task_id") or "") != task_id:
        continue

Split it so a GOAL-LEVEL ledger of this task's own goal is accepted while every foreign reference stays rejected:

    entry_goal = str(entry.get("goal_id") or "")
    entry_task = str(entry.get("task_id") or "")
    if entry_goal != goal_id:
        continue          # foreign goal: never
    if entry_task and entry_task != task_id:
        continue          # a DIFFERENT task's ledger: never
    # entry_task empty -> a goal-level ledger of this goal (e.g. cmd_goal_complete's
    # type:completion entry, whose evidence cites .shiki/reports/R-*.json)

Leave the `.shiki/`-prefix check and the resolve-and-contain check on each evidence ref exactly as they are. Update the docstring: it currently states the bound as 'goal_id AND task_id match', which will no longer be accurate.

Add `tests/test_completion_lock_scope.py` covering, against `_derive_task_mirror_locks` and through the files-outside-locks gate:
  - a goal-level completion ledger (goal_id matches, task_id null) whose evidence cites `.shiki/reports/R-*.json` -> both the ledger path and the report path appear in the derived locks;
  - the same ledger with a FOREIGN goal_id -> contributes nothing;
  - a ledger with a DIFFERENT task_id but the right goal_id -> contributes nothing (this is the anti-padding property; it must not regress);
  - a goal-level ledger whose evidence ref escapes the subtree (`.shiki/../outside.json`) -> contributes nothing;
  - a goal-level ledger whose evidence ref is not `.shiki/`-prefixed -> contributes nothing;
  - an end-to-end case shaped like PR #199: a task with three named-file locks, a closeout diff containing the task/lock/worktree/goal files plus a completion ledger and its scorecard, returns no 'outside declared task locks' blocker.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: a closeout PR that completes its goal blocks with `Changed file .shiki/ledger/L-<id>.json is outside declared task locks` and `Changed file .shiki/reports/R-<id>.json is outside declared task locks`, even though the ledger IS listed in the task's own `ledger_evidence` and the report is the evidence that ledger cites.
  Root cause: `_derive_task_mirror_locks` requires a ledger's `task_id` to equal the task's id before expanding it. `cmd_goal_complete` writes the completion ledger at GOAL level with `task_id: null`, so the ledger is skipped and its scorecard reference is never derived.
  Why it appeared only now: closeout PR #185 carried the identical pair and merged, because its task declared `path:.shiki/**`. The lock-narrowing discipline (ADR 0016) replaced directory globs with named files, so nothing masks the gap any more. Every goal-completing closeout is now unmergeable.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: in `_derive_task_mirror_locks`, replace the single combined goal_id/task_id inequality with a foreign-goal rejection plus a `if entry_task and entry_task != task_id` rejection, so an empty `task_id` on a same-goal ledger is accepted.
  Manual step removed: hand-editing a stale lock record, or re-widening a task's locks to `.shiki/**`, to get a closeout merged.
  Observed: PR #199, MergeGate metadata check, blocking_reasons naming exactly `.shiki/ledger/L-20260730T014952356458Z-646217d8.json` and `.shiki/reports/R-20260730T014952341651Z-aa477a7e.json`; the completion ledger reads `type: completion, goal_id: G-20260729T092307426018Z-584fb95e, task_id: None, evidence: ['.shiki/reports/R-20260730T014952341651Z-aa477a7e.json']`.
  Reproducible when: `shiki loop step` can drive a goal-completing closeout to merge with no operator lock surgery, and the anti-padding tests still reject foreign-goal and foreign-task ledgers.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Cover the goal-completion ledger and its scorecard in the derived mirror locks
